Greater Omaha Packing Co., Inc.
Risk Management Plan (RMP)  Executive Summary
________________________________________
A. Accidental Release Prevention and Safety Policies
Greater Omaha Packing Co., Inc. (GOP) is committed to maintaining the highest standards in chemical safety and accident prevention. Our facilitys ammonia refrigeration system includes prevention and mitigation measures that align with 40 CFR Part 68, Section 7.4(e), and Process Safety Management (PSM) principles. 
These include:
	Engineering Controls
o	Vents
o	Relief valves
o	Check valves
o	Manual and automatic shutoffs
o	Interlocks and alarms
o	Purge systems
o	Emergency air supply systems
	Training and Procedures
o	All personnel involved with ammonia systems receive initial and annual refresher training.
o	Standard operating procedures (SOPs) are in place for safe operation and maintenance.
	Maintenance and Integrity Programs
o	Equipment inspections are performed on hourly, daily, weekly, and monthly cycles.
o	A preventive maintenance program ensures timely servicing and replacement before any system degradation.
________________________________________
B. Stationary Source Description
The regulated substance at this facility is anhydrous ammonia (CAS #7664-41-7), used in our industrial refrigeration system. The total inventory exceeds the 10,000-pound threshold requiring an RMP. The primary stationary source is the ammonia receiver, located on the south side of the plant.
________________________________________
C. General and Chemical-Specific Prevention Measures
	Compliance with Section 7.4(e) of the RMP and PSM
	Training for refrigeration system employees
	Preventive maintenance on all critical components
	Use of ammonia-rated equipment and materials only
	Regular inspections and testing in line with manufacturer and regulatory recommendations
________________________________________
D. Five-Year Accident History
Greater Omaha Packing Co., Inc. has not experienced any accidental rel

eases of regulated substances resulting in offsite impacts in the past five years.
________________________________________
E. Emergency Response Program and Coordination
The Emergency Action Plan (EAP) for Greater Omaha Packing is designed to protect employees, visitors, contractors, the surrounding community, and the environment from the consequences of accidental chemical releases. Our program includes:
	Emergency Evacuation Procedures
o	Clearly posted evacuation maps throughout the facility
o	Department supervisors conduct roll-call at designated assembly areas
o	Emergency response drills and annual EAP training for all employees
	Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and Respiratory Protection
o	Trained responders equipped with gas masks/respirators per ANSI Z99.2-1969
o	Written procedures for safe respirator use and rescue response
	Coordination with Local Emergency Responders
o	Omaha Police Department  Site security and traffic control
o	Omaha Fire Department  Emergency rescue operations
o	Local Emergency Planning Committee (LEPC) and Nebraska SERC
o	Media notification and public protective action guidance
	Team Assignment Checklists for Ammonia Release  Fabrication & Slaughter Departments
o	Roles include evacuation coordination, emergency services contact, personnel accountability, containment actions, external communications, documentation, and recovery operations.
________________________________________
F. Continuous Improvement and Commitment
Greater Omaha Packing Co., Inc. remains dedicated to continuous improvement in process safety and environmental protection. The absence of accidental releases over the past five years reflects the effectiveness of our programs. Moving forward, GOP will maintain and enhance:
	Preventive maintenance schedules
	Employee training and certification
	Incident response drills
	Interagency coordination and communication
